THE CHALLENGE

Industrial data is everywhere — and nowhere.

Most plants run on a patchwork of PLCs, drives, weighing scales, energy meters, printers and sensors. Each speaks a different protocol, none of them talk to the cloud, and operations teams pay the price in blind spots.

01 / 04
Stranded sensor data

Modbus and serial devices speak their own language. Cloud platforms speak HTTP/MQTT. Without a bridge, the data never leaves the panel.

02 / 04
Brittle connectivity

A single carrier and a fragile radio means lost telemetry every time the link drops — and no record of what happened in between.

03 / 04
No edge intelligence

Vanilla loggers only push raw values. Operators want first-pass rules, alerts, and local control without waiting on a round trip.

04 / 04
Closed boxes

Off-the-shelf gateways force their own firmware, their own cloud, and their own pricing model — making integration a vendor lock-in problem.

A bridge built for plants, not pilots.

One ruggedised box that speaks every industrial protocol on the floor, talks to every carrier on the roof, and survives the times when neither side is co-operating.

TWO SENSORS, ONE GATEWAY

An authoritative gate, and a second set of eyes.

AID-Auto ships as two complementary units. The active breath test is the only authority that decides whether the vehicle may start; the passive cabin sensor only ever adds context. Deploy the active unit on its own, or run both for layered assurance.

ELECTROCHEMICAL FUEL CELL

Active Driver Breath Test

The driver blows a directed sample. Firmware integrates the current-versus-time curve and maps it to a breath-alcohol figure compared against your configured limit.

Strongly ethanol-selective — ignores common cabin interferents
Evidential-grade go / no-go accuracy
Effectively instant-on — no heater warm-up
Blow validation + driver-presence confirmation
Negligible power at rest; energised only during a test
BEST ROLE
Authoritative pre-ignition gate
SUPPLEMENTARY · CONTEXT
AID-Auto
CABIN SENSOR

HEATED SEMICONDUCTOR (MOS)

Passive Cabin Sniffing

A heated metal-oxide film continuously samples cabin air and raises a flag when alcohol-like vapour crosses a baseline. No directed sample, no driver action.

Always-on; no action required from any occupant
Low cost and mechanically simple
Flags alcohol-like vapour anywhere in the cabin
Cross-sensitive — sanitiser, fuel, perfume, smoke
Indicative only — never a standalone gate
BEST ROLE
Supplementary cabin anomaly flag

Hybrid by design. Only the active breath test can permit or block a start. The passive sensor never gates the vehicle — it is attached to events as a clearly-labelled cabin signal, never the decision.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

Accurate where it counts. Auditable everywhere.

The engineering value is not in reading alcohol — that part is easy — but in reading it accurately, attributing it to the driver, and behaving safely and tamper-evidently in a real vehicle.

Block an impaired start before ignition

Evidential fuel-cell breath accuracy

Fail-safe interlock — only ever prevents starting

Tamper- and bypass-evident by design

Every test logged with timestamp & location

Real-time alerts to your fleet desk

Proudly designed & made in India

HOW IT WORKS

Two channels. Only one decides.

Both sensing channels terminate at a shared low-power edge controller. The active result is always the deciding value; the passive cabin reading is attached only as context.

ACTIVE PATH — THE GATE

A directed breath, scored against your limit

1

Directed breath

Driver blows a real, sustained sample. Blow validation rejects ambient air or a substitute source.

2

Integrate the curve

Firmware captures the current-vs-time curve of the breath and integrates it — never a single instantaneous value.

3

Compare to threshold

The result maps to a breath-alcohol figure and is compared against your configured, remotely-set limit.

4

Start-permit decision

Below limit → start-permit enabled. At or above → start withheld, alert raised, event logged.

PASSIVE PATH — CONTEXT

A continuous read of the cabin air

1

Sample cabin air

A heated metal-oxide film sits in the cabin atmosphere — no directed sample, no occupant action.

2

Resistance shifts

Reducing vapour alters the film resistance; firmware reads the relative trend continuously.

3

Anomaly flag

Crossing a configured baseline raises an "alcohol-like vapour" flag — indicative, not quantitative.

4

Context only

The flag is attached to events for review. It never permits or blocks a start.

COMPARATIVE ASSESSMENT

Why the active channel holds the keys.

The two approaches differ across every attribute that determines suitability for an ignition-gating product. The matrix makes the division of labour explicit.

ATTRIBUTE	
PRIMARY · GATE
Active — Driver Breath Test
	
SUPPLEMENTARY

Sensing principle	Electrochemical fuel cell — ethanol oxidised at a catalytic electrode	Heated semiconductor metal-oxide film whose resistance changes with reducing vapour
What it measures	Breath alcohol from a directed sample, attributable to the driver	Aggregate alcohol-like vapour anywhere in the cabin air
Selectivity	High — strongly ethanol-selective	Low — also responds to sanitiser, perfume, fuel, smoke
Quantitative accuracy	Evidential-grade; supports a calibrated go / no-go threshold	Indicative only; not a trustworthy absolute reading
Ready / warm-up	Effectively immediate; no heater to stabilise	Requires heater stabilisation before each reliable reading
Response time	Peak reading within a few seconds of a valid breath	Order of ten seconds, with a longer recovery tail
Attribution to driver	Strong, when paired with blow / presence validation	None — cannot distinguish driver from passenger or spill
Power draw	Negligible at rest; energised only during a test	Continuous heater load whenever sensing is active
Service life	Multiple years, then scheduled re-calibration	Shorter, with measurable drift requiring re-baselining
Best role	Authoritative pre-ignition gate	Supplementary cabin flag

Cellular SIM connectivity turns each local decision into a remotely-auditable event. Pass, fail or abort — with timestamp and location — reaches the AID-IOT fleet portal in near real time, with instant alerts on a failed test or a tamper condition.

THE PROBLEM
Shelf-life is invisible at the item level.

Warehouses write off stock they could have caught in time. Without item-level visibility, freshness is a guess — and recoverable inventory ends up as waste.

No per-item shelf-life

Stock is tracked by pallet or SKU, never by the individual unit that's actually about to expire.

Stale stock gets picked

Without FEFO at the bin, pickers grab whatever is nearest — older inventory keeps sinking to the back.

Manual paper receipts

Receipts are logged on paper. Timestamps are trusted on faith and easy to back-date.

Waste, no recovery

Expired stock is written off whole — yet roughly 48% was recoverable with earlier action.

NAVIC INTEGRATION

Authentic time, cryptographically bound to every litre.

1

A NavIC-compatible receiver module on the EDGE device locks onto the constellation.

2

The receiver delivers a 1-PPS signal and authenticated NMEA time stream to firmware.

3

Every transaction is timestamped using NavIC time — not the device's local clock.

4

The NavIC timestamp is cryptographically bound to the transaction before upload.

5

On signal loss, a disciplined oscillator holds time accuracy through the gap.

CONSTRAINT NODE DESIGN

A general-purpose computer is a liability. A constraint node is inert.

The EDGE device is purpose-locked at hardware, firmware, and network levels — it can perform exactly one mission and nothing else. This is not a software policy. It is structural.

SYSTEM AT A GLANCE

Three hardware layers, one private LoRa mesh.

Person tags broadcast GPS positions over LoRa. Fixed nodes and relay devices form the mesh that carries packets across the locality. A gateway relay device forwards data to the local server that drives the live dashboard.

FIGURE — TRACKNET HARDWARE COMPONENTS AND COMMUNICATION LINKS

LAYER 1

Tracking

Person tag — card form, carried by the tracked individual. Broadcasts GPS position over LoRa at regular intervals.

LAYER 2

Infrastructure

Fixed nodes (solar) and rugged handheld relay devices form a self-healing LoRa mesh covering the entire locality.

LAYER 3

Command

Local server receives packets from the gateway relay, processes events, and serves the live dashboard over the LAN.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES

Offline-first

Fully self-contained, no internet required.

GPS-derived

Position comes from the tag, not the network.

Mesh redundancy

Multi-hop routing survives node failures.

Configurable firmware

TX intervals, payload, power modes.

Scalable

Add fixed nodes incrementally as you grow.

USE CASES

Five operational scenarios, one tracking platform.

TrackNet is designed for any controlled locality where personnel movement must be visible — without depending on a mobile network or cloud service.

Personnel Tracking in Restricted Areas
Track authorised personnel inside compounds, campuses, or industrial sites
Block unauthorised entry into restricted or hazardous zones
Real-time visibility to a central security desk — no mobile network needed
Security Patrol Monitoring
Monitor patrol routes of security personnel carrying relay devices
Verify patrol coverage of all designated checkpoints
Detect deviations from assigned routes and trigger alerts
Event & Crowd Management
Track registered participants or VIPs at events and exhibitions
Identify crowd concentrations and movement patterns
Coordinate evacuations using the last-known position of every tagged person
Construction & Industrial Site Safety
Monitor worker locations across large sites and warehouses
Account for all personnel during emergencies or roll calls
Record zone entry/exit timestamps for compliance and audit
Educational or Institutional Campus
Track movement of students, staff, or visitors across a campus
Automate attendance via proximity to fixed nodes
Alert admins when a person enters an off-limits area

HOW IT WORKS

From tag transmission to dashboard update — seven steps, under 60 seconds.

End-to-end latency from a tag broadcast to a marker moving on the dashboard stays under one minute on a healthy mesh.

1

Tag transmits GPS position

The tag acquires a GPS fix and broadcasts a compact LoRa packet at the configured interval (default 30 s).

2

Mesh network relays the packet

The nearest fixed node or relay device receives the packet and hops it through the mesh toward the gateway.

3

Gateway delivers packet to local server

The gateway relay forwards the packet to the local server over USB serial or Bluetooth.

4

Location engine processes the packet

Determines the tag’s current zone, calculates movement state, and detects zone entry/exit events.

5

Event detection and alerting

Zone events or restricted-area violations log to the event store and can trigger dashboard alerts.

6

Dashboard receives live update

The dashboard API pushes the new position to connected browsers over WebSocket — markers move in real time.

7

Data stored for audit and reporting

Positions and events persist to the local database for historical playback and compliance review.

HARDWARE

OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Built to operate under real-world conditions.

The conditions TrackNet must reliably meet in the field — from offline networks to overnight power and multi-user access.

Network & Connectivity

Operates entirely offline — no SIM, no cellular, no internet. All communication uses LoRa radio (862–930 MHz) with a self-healing mesh.

Coverage & Range

Fixed nodes provide overlapping coverage across the locality. Typical open-area range is 1–5 km per hop. Relay devices extend coverage into unserved areas.

Update Frequency & Latency

Tags transmit at a configurable interval (default 30 s). End-to-end latency stays under 60 s under normal mesh conditions; stale tags are visually flagged.

Power & Durability

Scalability

Supports ≥ 50 simultaneous person tags per locality. Add fixed nodes incrementally to expand coverage — no reconfiguration of existing infrastructure.

From raw LoRa packet reception to dashboard visualisation — everything runs on the on-premise box. No external services in the data path.

STAGE 01

Packet Receiver

Connects to the gateway relay over USB serial or Bluetooth. Decodes LoRa packets — tag ID, GPS, RSSI, timestamp, battery — and publishes to an internal broker. Auto-reconnects on disconnect.

STAGE 02

Location Processing Engine

Subscribes to the receiver, applies zone detection from configured boundaries, computes movement state (moving / idle / offline), detects entry/exit events, and writes positions to the database.

STAGE 03

Local Database

SQLite (default) or PostgreSQL for larger deployments. Stores positions, zone events, infrastructure status, and user config — with a configurable rolling retention (default 30 days).

STAGE 04

Dashboard API & Web Server

REST API plus WebSocket / SSE for live updates. Serves the single-page dashboard on the LAN, handles authentication, RBAC, and session management.

This Privacy Policy explains how Inordinate Industrial Innovations Pvt Ltd (“AID-IoT”, “we”, “us” or “our”) collects, uses, shares, and protects your personal information when you visit aid-iot.com (the “Site”), contact us, subscribe to our newsletter, or purchase products through our online store. Information you provide to us

- Newsletter: when you subscribe, we collect your email address.
- Contact / enquiry forms: when you reach out to us, we collect your name, email address, phone number (if provided), and the contents of your message.

Information we collect automatically

When you visit the Site, we may automatically collect certain technical information about your device and usage, such as your IP address, browser type, device type, time zone, referring pages, and how you interact with the Site. We refer to this as “Usage Information” and collect it using cookies and similar technologies (see “Cookies” below).

HOW WE USE YOUR INFORMATION

We use your personal information to:

- Respond to your enquiries and provide customer support;
- Send you our newsletter and product updates where you have subscribed (you may unsubscribe at any time);
- Process, fulfil, and deliver your orders, including sending invoices and order confirmations;
- Operate, maintain, secure, and improve the Site, and prevent fraud or abuse;
- Comply with our legal and regulatory obligations.

COOKIES

We use cookies and similar technologies to keep the Site functioning, remember your preferences, and understand how the Site is used. You can control or disable cookies through your browser settings; some features of the Site may not function properly without them.

PAYMENTS

Online payments on our store are processed by Razorpay, a third-party payment gateway. Your payment is handled securely by Razorpay in accordance with its own privacy policy and applicable card-network security standards. We receive confirmation of your transaction but do not collect or store your complete card, UPI, or banking credentials.

HOW WE SHARE YOUR INFORMATION

We do not sell your personal information. We share it only with trusted service providers who help us operate the Site and our business, and only to the extent necessary, including:

- Razorpay — payment processing;
- Google reCAPTCHA — to protect our forms from spam and abuse (subject to Google’s Privacy Policy and Terms);
- Our email, hosting, and analytics providers — to deliver communications and run the Site;
- Authorities or third parties where required by law, regulation, legal process, or to protect our rights.

DATA RETENTION

We retain your personal information only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes described in this policy, to comply with our legal, accounting, or reporting obligations, and to resolve disputes. You may request deletion of your information as described under “Your Rights”.

DATA SECURITY

We implement reasonable technical and organisational measures designed to protect your personal information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. However, no method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

YOUR RIGHTS

Subject to applicable law, including the DPDP Act, 2023, you have the right to access, correct, update, or request deletion of your personal information, and to withdraw consent where processing is based on consent. To exercise these rights, please contact us using the details below. We may need to verify your identity before acting on your request.

CHILDREN’S PRIVACY

The Site is intended for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us so we can delete it.

CHANGES TO THIS POLICY

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or for legal reasons. The “Last updated” date above indicates when it was last revised. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

PROGRAMME OVERVIEW

Learn to fly safely, legally and with confidence.

The Drone Pilot programme takes participants from zero stick-time to controlled, regulation-aware flight. It blends ground school, simulator practice and supervised field sessions so trainees understand not only how to fly, but when, where and how to fly responsibly.

DURATION

3 days

Ground school, simulator and supervised flight

COHORT SIZE

Small batches

High instructor-to-trainee ratio at the field

FRAMEWORK

DGCA-aligned

Mapped to small-category remote-pilot norms

ON COMPLETION

Certificate

Safety-first by design

Airspace, weather & failsafe literacy

GROUND SCHOOL

Everything that happens before the props spin.

Six structured modules build the knowledge a responsible remote pilot needs — long before take-off. Theory is delivered alongside simulator drills so concepts stick.

01

Airspace & regulation

Drone categories, no-fly and restricted zones, the Digital Sky framework and the rules that govern where and when you may operate.

02

Aerodynamics & systems

How a multirotor stays in the air, the role of each onboard subsystem, and how propulsion, sensing and control work together.

03

Ground control & telemetry

Reading the GCS, interpreting live telemetry, GPS lock, battery and link health before and during every flight.

04

Weather & site assessment

Wind limits, visibility, interference sources and how to survey and clear a site before take-off.

05

Manual & assisted flight

Stick discipline in stabilise, altitude-hold and loiter modes — the foundation of precise, repeatable control.

06

Emergencies & failsafe

Return-to-home, low-battery and link-loss behaviour, and the decision-making for a safe abort or recovery.

FIELD TRAINING

Stick-time that builds real confidence.

Trainees progress through four supervised stages, only advancing once the previous one is solid. The result is a pilot who flies smoothly — and knows exactly what to do when something goes wrong.

1

Simulator drills

Repeatable muscle-memory practice with zero risk — orientation, hover and recovery before touching a real aircraft.

2

Tethered & low hover

First powered flights at low altitude under direct instructor supervision, focused on smooth, controlled inputs.

3

Pattern flying

Box patterns, figure-eights and orientation changes to build true spatial awareness and confident control.

4

Mission & waypoints

Planning and flying an autonomous waypoint mission while monitoring telemetry and staying ready to intervene.

LEARNING OUTCOMES

What graduates can do.

On completion of the programme, every trainee will be able to:

Interpret airspace rules and identify where flight is permitted or restricted.

Perform a complete pre-flight inspection and site assessment.

Fly a multirotor confidently in stabilise, altitude-hold and loiter modes.

Read and act on live telemetry — GPS, battery, signal and attitude.

Plan and execute a basic autonomous waypoint mission.

Respond correctly to link-loss, low-battery and other in-flight emergencies.

WHO IT'S FOR

For everyone who needs a steady hand on the sticks.

No previous flight experience is required. Trainees who already fly are streamed into a faster track focused on precision and emergency handling.

Anyone starting their journey toward responsible recreational or academic flying.

Survey & mapping teams

Professionals who need reliable, repeatable flight for aerial data capture.

Inspection & operations

Field teams adopting drones for infrastructure, agriculture or asset inspection.

Research groups

Labs operating UAV platforms who want a safe, standardised piloting baseline.

ON YOUR EQUIPMENT

Every station in the IdeaLab, put to work.

The programme is mapped to the standard IdeaLab toolset — so faculty learn on the exact machines their students will use. Nothing here needs gear you don't already have.

FDM 3D printers

Print airframe arms, motor mounts, camera pods and jigs in PLA, PETG and nylon — iterate a part in an afternoon.

Laser cutter

Cut and engrave acrylic, ply and composite plates for frames, mounting decks and assembly fixtures with precision.

Desktop CNC

Machine carbon-fibre and aluminium parts where strength and stiffness matter most on the airframe.

Electronics bench

Soldering stations, bench supplies and meters for wiring power distribution, ESCs and the flight controller.

CAD & slicer suite

Parametric CAD and slicing workflow so a design change flows cleanly through to a printable, cuttable part.

Test & measurement

Thrust stands, oscilloscopes and loggers to characterise motors, props and power before the first flight.

One drone, six stations, start to finish.

Faculty carry a single aircraft through the entire prototyping pipeline — the same arc they'll later guide their students through.

01

Concept & CAD

Define mission and payload, then model the airframe parametrically so every part is ready to fabricate.

02

Fabricate parts

Print, laser-cut and machine the frame, mounts and fixtures — and learn the design-for-fabrication trade-offs first-hand.

03

Assemble & wire

Integrate motors, ESCs, power distribution and the flight controller into a clean, serviceable build.

04

Configure & calibrate

Flash firmware, calibrate sensors and set flight modes — the bridge from a static frame to a flyable aircraft.

05

Test & validate

Bench-test thrust and power, run pre-flight checks, then a supervised hover to validate the complete build.

06

Take it to students

A ready-to-run lab plan, part library and rubric so faculty can deliver the same build in their own courses.

On completion of the FDP, every participating faculty member will be able to:

Operate IdeaLab fabrication equipment confidently for UAV parts.

Take a drone from CAD concept through to a flyable, tested prototype.

Apply design-for-fabrication thinking across printing, cutting and machining.

Integrate, wire and calibrate a complete multirotor system.

Run pre-flight checks and a safe, supervised validation flight.

Deliver the same hands-on build to their own students with provided lab material.
